item.title: Funeral Home / Blue Monkey
item.description:
Some things never rest in peace… When the easily scared Heather (Lesleh Donaldson) comes to town to help her grandmother turn a decaying funeral home into a charming bed-and-breakfast, strange happenings and unexplained murders begin to threaten their plans. Will Heather be able to work up the courage to investigate the funeral home’s dark and mysterious past? More importantly, will she survive long enough to solve the mystery? Long available only on video, William Fruet’s Funeral Home (also known as Cries in the Night ) is an essential yet underseen piece of Canadian horror history. (American Genre Film Archive) “Fruet once again proves himself a deft director, with natural camera movements and a good eye for composition [in Funeral Home ].” – Canuxploitation.com They breed, they hatch, they kill! William Fruet’s Blue Monkey is a fast-paced monster movie updating the nuclear paranoia / big bug sci-fi horror flicks of the ’50s with ultra-gooey ’80s practical effects. When a worm-like beast is birthed at a hospital following a greenhouse accident, detective Steve Railsback must contain the creature before it transforms into an unstoppable killing machine. “[ Blue Monkey ] is a fun outing for Canadian director William Fruet, who succeeds not only by drawing a campy playfulness from his material, but also in scoring some brilliant casting. It goes straight for the jugular.” – Canuxploitation.com

item.title: The Beyond / Pieces
item.description:
Woe be unto him who opens one of the seven gateways to Hell, because through that gateway, evil will invade the world. Italian horror icon Lucio Fulci unleashes his towering terror masterpiece, a fright-filled, gore-soaked fever dream that follows a young woman (frequent Fulci star Catriona MacColl), whose recently inherited old Louisianian hotel holds dark secrets. Long available only in an edited, incomplete version, The Beyond was beautifully restored & rereleased uncut in the late ‘90s by Grindhouse Releasing and Quentin Tarantino’s Rolling Thunder Pictures. You don’t have to go to Texas for a chainsaw massacre! The pinnacle of enthusiastically bloodthirsty, deliriously entertaining slasher sickies, Juan Piquer Simón’s Pieces continues to pack a punch 40 plus years after it first splattered grindhouse screens. As a college campus is terrorized by a deranged madman hacking up co-eds, a detective & an uncover cop (real-life husband & wife Christopher & Lynda Day George) must solve the deadly puzzle.

item.title: Homicidal / Mr. Sardonicus
item.description:
In the small town of Solvang, there’s a killer on the loose… and a bizarre household may hold the key to murder. Nurse Emily takes care of her husband Warren’s childhood guardian, a wheelchair-bound stroke victim. But this nurse’s bedside manner is to die for. As Warren’s half-sister closes in on the truth, she uncovers a town’s most chilling mystery… and her family’s darkest secret. (Sony) Desperate to retrieve a winning lottery ticket, a greedy baron unearths his father’s corpse. An enormous jackpot is his reward, but not without a price: his face is frozen permanently into a hideous grin. He enlists his fiendish one-eyed servant to help him lift this horrible curse, but their schemes fail. Finally, he turns to a noted neurosurgeon – and his wife’s former lover – to cure him. This creepy horror classic is based on a novella by screenwriter Ray Russell, and is brought to life by William Castle, master of terror! (Sony)

item.title: Beetlejuice
item.description:
Tim Burton’s afterlife spooktacular is an energetic mix of goth fantasy and laugh-out-loud comedy! When two newlyweds (Geena Davis & Alec Baldwin) die in a car accident, they must haunt their recently departed home and scare away the obnoxious replacement residents (Jeffrey Jones & Catherine O’Hara), while befriending the new tenants’ teenage daughter (Winona Ryder). But they get more trouble than they bargained for when they recruit Michael Keaton’s rambunctious “bio-exorcist” Beetlejuice to help.

item.title: Halloween: H20
item.description:
Twenty years after the horrific events of Halloween , Laurie Strode must battle the Shape one last time. Jamie Lee Curtis triumphantly returns to the role that made her a scream queen, playing Strode as a woman haunted by her past and living under an assumed name as the headmistress of a private boarding school. But when her rebellious son and his friends skip their school trip to party on the quiet campus, knife-wielding maniac Michael Myers sees them as perfect victims for his belated bloodbath. A game cast of fresh faces, including Josh Hartnett, Michelle Williams, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, and Jodi Lyn O’Keefe, co-star alongside LL Cool J and Janet Leigh. “ Halloween: H20 is as stylish and scary as it is ultra-violent. It brings back a stunning Jamie Lee Curtis in the role that made her a star and it’s a work of superior craftsmanship in all aspects.” – Kevin Thomas, Los Angeles Times

item.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
item.description:
A new kind of horror remake from Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ), starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium. (MUBI)

item.title: The Others / The Orphanage
item.description:
In 1945, Grace Stewart (Nicole Kidman) and her two children live an unusually isolated existence behind the locked doors and drawn curtains of a secluded mansion on one of the Channel Islands. The arrival of mysterious new servants (Fionnula Flanagan, Ed Sykes) and her apparently war-fatigued husband Charles (Christopher Eccleston), raise the unworldly feeling that there is far more to this house than can be seen, provoking Grace into a terrifying fight to save her children and preserve her sanity. (Rialto Pictures) Award-winning visionary Guillermo del Toro and acclaimed director J.A. Bayona present a “positively terrifying” (John Anderson, Newsday) new vision of the classic ghost story. Returning to her childhood home – a mysterious, seaside orphanage – Laura and her family unknowingly unleash a long-forgotten evil spirit. Now thrust into a chilling nightmare, Laura must confront the memories of her past before the ghosts of the orphanage destroy her… and everything she has ever loved. (New Line Cinema)

item.title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (Silent with Live Music Score)
item.description:
While our allotment of advance tickets has sold out online, some additional tickets will be available to purchase at the door on a first come, first served basis on the night of the show. Box office & doors open roughly one hour before showtime. For shows that have sold out online, in-person ticket purchases are limited to 2 tickets per person. Featuring live musical accompaniment by Cliff Retallick In 1920, one brilliant movie jolted the postwar masses and catapulted the German Expressionist film movement into history. That movie was The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari , a plunge into the mind of insanity that severs all ties with the rational world. Director Robert Wiene and a team of visionary designers crafted a nightmare realm in which light, shadow and substance are abstracted, a world in which a demented doctor and a carnival sleepwalker perpetrate a series of ghastly murders in a small community. (Kino Lorber)
Cast: Director: Robert Wiene | Starring: Werner Krauss, Conrad Veidt, Friedrich Fehér, Lil Dagover | Year: 1920 | Country: Germany | Format: 35mm
Durata: 75 minuti

item.title: From Dusk Till Dawn
item.description:
George Clooney and Quentin Tarantino star as brothers on the lam from the law, hightailing it to Mexico with a kidnapped family in tow. But when they stop at an isolated strip club, they’ll have to try and survive From Dusk Till Dawn while battling the bar’s bloodthirsty denizens in Robert Rodriguez’s pulpy, stylish & hyper-violent cross-genre blast penned by its co-star. Featuring Harvey Keitel, Juliette Lewis & Salma Hayek plus an all-star cast of character actor greats including Cheech Marin, Fred Williamson, Danny Trejo and Tom Savini! “It’s easy to imagine From Dusk Till Dawn as the all-time favorite film of Christian Slater’s film-geek character in True Romance . A deliriously trashy, exuberantly vulgar, lavishly appointed exploitation picture, a weird combo of roadkill movie and martial-arts vampire gorefest” – Variety

item.title: The Fly (1986)
item.description:
A big screen love story unlike anything you’ve ever seen, David Cronenberg’s ‘80s update of The Fly is as terrifyingly tragic as its ultra-gooey Oscar-winning special effects are jaw-droppingly grotesque. When an eccentric scientist (Jeff Goldblum) uses himself as a test subject, he soon discovers himself devolving into something not quite human, with disastrous consequences to the relationship with his reporter girlfriend (Geena Davis). Bringing his body horror fascination to the mainstream, Cronenberg crafts a gross-out masterpiece that targets the heart as well as the stomach. “ The Exorcist aside, I can’t think of another horror film as intense as The Fly . They are both almost unbearable to watch and certain sections of the latter have the upper-hand when it comes to inciting a sense of disgust, and that’s saying something.” – Roger Ebert “What makes The Fly such a stunning piece of obsessive film making is the way Cronenberg deftly allows us to identify with his monstrous creation.” -Patrick Goldstein, Los Angeles Times “A gross-your-eyes-out horror movie that is also the year’s most poignant romance.” – Richard Corliss, TIME Magazine
